title: Newark Home Energy Rebates 2026: PSE&G Heat Pump, Water Heater and Free Help
desc: Home energy rebates in Newark for 2026: PSE&G heat pump rebates up to $10,000, appliance and water heater rebates, a $5,000 battery rebate, and free weatherization for lower incomes.
lead: Newark is a city of renters, two-family buildings and older homes, and that shapes which rebates you can use. PSE&G pays for heat pumps, water heaters, appliances and a home battery, and the state pays for free weatherization. The federal tax credits are gone. This page sorts the money by who you are in Newark: an owner, a renter or a lower-income household. We read each program's own page on October 6, 2026.
cards_heading: What is open in Newark in 2026
cards_intro: Each card names the fact we keep on file, with the date we last read the official page. PSE&G can change or end its programs without notice.

cards.title: Heat pump that replaces gas, oil or propane
cards.note: For owners of homes of one to four units. Income-qualified homes can get up to $12,000. Read the Newark heat pump guide.

cards.title: Standard heat pump
cards.note: Instant rebate on the contractor's invoice, by efficiency tier. Extra $300 if you are income-qualified.

cards.title: Heat pump water heater
cards.note: $750 when it replaces a gas or oil water heater, $450 on the standard list. See the water heater guide.

cards.title: Appliance rebates
cards.note: Induction cooktop $250, electric dryer up to $300, washer up to $100, refrigerator up to $100. Apply within 120 days of purchase. See the appliance guide.

cards.title: GridSmart home battery
cards.note: For owners who want backup power. New installs only, and you let PSE&G use the battery for up to 100 events a year. See the battery guide.

cards.title: PSE&G Home Weatherization
cards.note: Free assessment, products and insulation work for households between 250% and 400% of the poverty level, in a moderate-income area, in NJ SHARES or in an overburdened community.

cards.title: Comfort Partners
cards.note: State program for households at or below 250% of the poverty level, in buildings of 14 or fewer units. Call 866-378-4345.

cards.title: Federal 25C and 25D credits
cards.note: No federal credit applies to work done after December 31, 2025.

after_cards: Most of these programs are described in more detail on our PSE&G rebates page, which lists every card with the date we last read it.
sections:
The Census Bureau's American Community Survey (2020 to 2024) counts 121,546 homes in Newark, and 113,384 are someone's usual home. Renters live in 75.6% of them and owners in 24.4%. Buildings with two to four homes make up 40.6% of the city's housing, detached houses 12.6% and attached houses such as rowhouses 10.6%. The rest are larger apartment buildings.

That mix means a Newark rebate usually has two people behind it: an owner who can apply and a tenant who lives with the result. The sections below say who does what.
If you own a one- to four-family building

PSE&G's decarbonization rules cover single-family and attached homes of one to four units, as long as you own the home. That includes the two-family house, which is the most common building type in Newark. You can use the heat pump, water heater and battery rebates, and the on-bill repayment option spreads the cost over your PSE&G bills with no interest. The company requires 12 months of on-time payments, with no credit check.

Tenants cannot apply for the heat pump rebates, because the program asks for the owner of the house. You still have options. The appliance rebates are post-purchase and aimed at PSE&G customers, and the free Whole Home Energy Assessment can bring a free smart thermostat and small products into your home. Check the terms before you buy, and ask your landlord before changing anything fixed to the building. If your household income is low, call Comfort Partners.

Utility gas heats 68.3% of homes, electricity 22.6%, bottled gas 2.8% and fuel oil 2.5%. Gas and oil homes can use the large replacement rebate. Electric-heat homes use the standard instant rebate and the heat pump water heater rebate. About 65.6% of Newark's homes were built before 1980 and 23.7% before 1940, so a contractor should check insulation and ductwork before sizing any equipment. Free weatherization first can make a smaller, cheaper heat pump enough.

Two free programs can reach Newark households. PSE&G Home Weatherization covers households with income between 250% and 400% of the federal poverty level, those in moderate-income areas, NJ SHARES members and overburdened communities. Comfort Partners covers households at or below 250% of poverty, or on SNAP, Section 8, SSI, TANF or General Assistance. Both can include insulation and air sealing at no cost. Call one and let them route you.
claim_heading: How to get started in Newark
claim_steps: Look at your electric bill to confirm PSE&G is the company.
Decide whether you are an owner, a renter or a lower-income household using the sections above.
Owners: call PSE&G's program line at 1-855-846-2895 and ask for a participating contractor.
Renters and lower incomes: ask for the free Whole Home Energy Assessment or call Comfort Partners.
Keep every invoice and model number.
faq: Yes. Newark appears in Essex County on PSE&G's official service territory list, for both electric and gas.
I rent in Newark. Can I get a heat pump rebate?
Not on your own. The program asks for the owner of the house. You can use appliance rebates and free weatherization if you qualify.
Is there a rebate for a two-family house?
Yes, if you own it. PSE&G's rules cover homes of one to four units.
Are federal tax credits still open?
No. The 25C and 25D credits ended for work done after December 31, 2025.
Where can I run the numbers?
Use our New Jersey rebate calculator and pick PSE&G as your utility.
